title: prefill-decode-stage-overlap-chunked-speculative-kernel-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and improve throughput for common chat workloads by better overlapping prefill and decode stages, splitting large prefill requests into chunked units that schedule more favorably on the kernel scheduler, and applying speculative prefill execution for high-confidence token prefixes. This PR combines changes across the prefill pipeline, kernel scheduler, KV cache memory accounting, and continuous batching.

Summary of changes: implement chunked prefill executor (splits long sequences into N-sized chunks and schedules them in a stage-overlap-friendly way), add speculative prefill path that issues tentative decode work for top-k prefixes when confidence > threshold, refactor kernel scheduler to incorporate stage-affinity and chunk-aware slotting, and reduce KV cache lock contention and memory fragmentation with a segment pool and LRU shard hints. Also add telemetry (per-route prefill/chunk latency, speculative success/fallback rate, kv-cache hit/eviction counters) and a config flag to gate speculative prefill.

Checklist:
- [x] Chunked prefill executor implementation and unit tests
- [x] Speculative prefill path + safety fallbacks and tests
- [x] Kernel scheduler heuristics for chunk affinity
- [x] KV cache segment pool + eviction tuning
- [x] Continuous batcher integration and low-latency benchmarks
- [x] Docs: ops runbook for tuning chunk size and speculative threshold
- [x] CI: linux build + perf tests

Impact: On representative web-chat workloads (avg prefill length 512 tokens, concurrent users 200), we observe 8-15% higher throughput at 95th-pctl latency unchanged or slightly improved, and an estimated per-token cost reduction of ~12% due to better GPU utilization and fewer decode retries. Speculative prefill yields a net improvement when applied to stable models (GPT-like architectures) with a conservative threshold; the path is disabled by default behind a feature flag.

Notes and compatibility: The change is backwards-compatible for API consumers. Admins/operators can tune chunk_size and speculative_threshold via runtime config. The KV cache pool changes require a rolling restart to avoid transient double-allocation; operator notes are in docs/ops/prefill_tuning.md.

Related: ENG-1842 (prefill pipeline perf epics), ENG-1907 (kernel scheduler improvements), referenced earlier prefill/decode stage overlap PRs listed in repo history.

review_comments: Linus Chen: Please add per-chunk telemetry and a knob to disable chunking per-route. Also call out memory overhead in the PR description - otherwise LGTM.

release_notes: Performance: improved prefill-decode overlap via chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and kernel scheduler affinity; reduced KV cache contention and memory fragmentation. Operators can tune chunk_size and speculative_threshold via runtime config. Backwards compatible; speculative prefill disabled by default.
perf_results_summary: 8-15% throughput improvement on web-chat workloads with avg prefill 512 tokens; ~12% per-token cost reduction estimate; speculative prefill net benefit when enabled for stable models.
operational_notes: Speculative prefill is behind feature flag 'prefill.speculative_enabled' (default: false).
Recommended chunk_size default: 64 for GPT-like models; tune based on latency SLOs and GPU occupancy.
KV cache segment pool bounded by 'kv.segment_pool_max_bytes' to avoid memory spikes; rolling restart recommended when toggling pool implementation.
New telemetry: prefill.chunk.latency_ms, prefill.speculative.success_rate, kv_cache.segment_evictions, kernel_scheduler.chunk_affinity_score.
